## Part 1 — fully worked: the spillway model

*A dam's spillway must pass a 900 m³/s design flood. The lab builds a
**1:36** Froude model (so √36 = 6 is the only arithmetic that matters).
Order the pump, set the clocks, and check the model's honesty.*

**Step 0 — which Π rules.** Free surface + gravity: Froude. (Re gets
policed, not matched — Step 3.) *Why this step exists:* choosing the wrong
ruling group is the only unrecoverable error in model testing.

**Step 1 — the pump order.** $Q \propto V \cdot A \propto \sqrt{L_r} \cdot L_r^2
= L_r^{5/2}$, so $Q_m = 900/36^{2.5} = 116$ L/s. A flood
becomes a fire hose.

**Step 2 — the clocks.** $t \propto L/V \propto \sqrt{L_r}$: model time
runs 6× fast. A 3-hour prototype flood plays out in 30 minutes of lab time.

**Step 3 — the honesty check.** Prototype flow ~8 m/s at 3 m depth → model
1.33 m/s at 8.3 cm. Model $Re \approx (1.33)(0.083)/10^{-6}
\approx 1.1\times10^5$: comfortably turbulent, so the friction physics is
the right *kind* even though Re isn't matched. Fr measured, Re policed —
the division of labor from module 2.2.

## Part 2 — the faded twin: the breakwater

*A harbor breakwater will face 12-second storm waves and ~8 m/s water
velocities at 10 m depth. The lab has a **1:25** wave basin (√25 = 5).*

**Step 0 on the house:** free surface again — Froude rules. You drive.

**What transferred.** Pick the ruling Π → √L for speeds and clocks → L³
for forces → police the abandoned number. Every hydraulic model report in
industry has these four sections, in this order, with these exponents.
:::

## Let the toolbox referee

```{pyodide}
#| autorun: false
from fluidtools.similitude import scale_report
scale_report('froude', 1/25)
print()
print(f"breakwater: t_m = {12/5:.1f} s, V_m = {8/5:.1f} m/s, F_p = {3.5*25**3:,.0f} N")
```
